title: Biscuits and Gravy
subtitle: American buttermilk biscuits with sausage cream gravy
excerpt: The Southern American breakfast staple: flaky, buttery buttermilk biscuits split open and smothered in a thick, peppered cream gravy made from crumbled pork sausage. Rich, deeply savoury, and resolutely unfussy.

recipe.sourceNotes: Biscuits and gravy is the definitive breakfast dish of the American South and a fixture across the Midwest. The biscuits are nothing like the British sweet biscuit: they are a leavened quick bread, related to a scone, made with cold butter or lard worked into flour and liquid until flaky. The gravy is a white country-style gravy thickened with flour and enriched with whole milk, not a stock-based sauce. The sausage used is American-style breakfast sausage: crumbled, highly seasoned pork sausage with sage and black pepper. Together, the combination is filling, cheap, and deeply savoury. It became popular as a peasant food in the post-Civil War South when meat was expensive and could be stretched by crumbling it into gravy served over starchy biscuits.

content.text: Keep the butter cold and work it into the flour quickly to keep the flakes in the biscuits. Do not overwork the dough or the biscuits will be tough. For the gravy, use plenty of black pepper: it is intentionally heavily seasoned. The gravy should be thick enough to coat a spoon; add more milk to loosen if needed.

squeeze meat from skins; for the gravy

content.text: Heat the oven to 220°C / fan 200°C / gas 7. Make the biscuits: combine flour, baking powder, and salt. Rub in the cold butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs with some larger flakes. Add the buttermilk and stir until just combined. Turn onto a floured surface, pat to 2.5 cm thick, and cut into rounds. Bake for 12 to 14 minutes until golden.

While the biscuits bake, make the gravy: fry the sausage meat in a large pan over medium-high heat, breaking it up, for 8 minutes until cooked through and browned in patches. Reduce the heat. Sprinkle the flour over and stir for 1 minute.

Pour in the milk gradually, stirring constantly. Add the sage and black pepper. Cook over medium heat, stirring, for 4 to 5 minutes until thick and creamy. Season with salt. To serve, split the warm biscuits and ladle the gravy over generously.
